{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABdCnCXQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhGk8NU", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 111, "title": "Handle legacy SCU DSTP MMIO without unsupported-access CPU halts", "body": "## Problem

A user testing their own 512 KiB Sega Saturn BIOS in **User-provided BIOS** mode can now pass the earlier SMPC `MissingSf` fault (Issue #109 / PR #110), but the firmware execution reaches this next fault:

```text
Memory access at PC 0x0000181E:
Unsupported Saturn device/register: 4-byte access at 0x05FE0060;
this build supports only the documented homebrew hardware subset
```

`0x05FE0060` is the SCU's historical **DSTP / DSTOP (DMA force-stop)** register, offset `+0x60`. The current diagnostic does not distinguish **read vs write** or a write value. The address may also be reached through SH-2 cached versus cache-through aliases or a generated cache-line access; **do not conclude that the BIOS directly executed a register write from the error text alone**.

At `main` `4e85a89a61e60886ce7b7055cf22fccb7e72c296`, `src/bus.rs` routes 4-byte accesses in the SCU range to `src/scu.rs::Scu::{read32,write32}`, both of which reject `+0x60` with `BusError::UnsupportedDevice`. The code cites ST-210 #14's prohibition of obsolete DSTOP functionality. This is an emulator-side fatal diagnostic, not evidence that the physical Saturn generates an SH-2 exception or halts on such an access.

The broader concern is architectural: **do not turn accesses that are undocumented, reserved, removed from a later specification, or unsupported by the emulator into automatic guest CPU termination unless hardware evidence warrants it**. Earlier/revision-dependent software may still access a legacy or unused register; some unknown accesses may be benign, while others must have real side effects. We need a principled compatibility policy, not a blanket ignore-all workaround.

## Primary sources and independent implementations

**Conflicting evidence must be documented rather than papered over:**

- Sega SCU User's Manual [ST-097-R5-072694](https://github.com/luckyseoul/saturn-docs/blob/main/files/ST-097-R5-072694.pdf): original DSTP register semantics.
- Sega [ST-210 final SCU specifications](https://github.com/luckyseoul/saturn-docs/blob/main/files/ST-210-110194.pdf), item 14: removes force-stop functionality and prohibits writes to DSTOP. Distinguish the final **programming restriction** from a verified CPU bus error or physical readback value. Check revision/production applicability.
- [Mednafen `scu.inc`](https://github.com/OpenEmu/Mednafen-Core/blob/master/mednafen/ss/scu.inc): `SCU_RegRW_DB` has `case 0x60` on writes, with a `TODO: Test`, stopping DMA channels when bit 0 is set; unknown reads return 0. This is not independent hardware measurement.
- [Yabause `scu.c`](https://github.com/Yabause/yabause/blob/master/yabause/src/scu.c): longword writes to `+0x60` retain `DSTP`; reads of this offset fall through to 0. The source does not demonstrate actual forced-stop effects.
- [5thPlanet `scu.rs`](https://github.com/hiroshiyui/5thPlanet/blob/main/crates/saturn/src/scu.rs): both reads and writes of DSTP are modeled as register storage; the round-trip unit test alone does not demonstrate DMA stop behavior.
- [MAME `saturn_scu.cpp`](https://github.com/mamedev/mame/blob/master/src/mame/sega/saturn_scu.cpp): `+0x60` force-stop mapping is commented out, unlike active DMA status register mapping.

There is **no demonstrated consensus on readback, electrical behavior or DMA stop side effects**, and no independently verified trace of the user's private BIOS. The implementer must not cargo-cult a single emulator's incomplete approximation.

## Expected outcome

Make an evidence-based, **narrow SCU DSTP compatibility correction**, with a reusable documented policy for **unsupported / obsolete / reserved MMIO accesses**: distinguish (1) actual hardware-observed software-visible behavior, (2) unknown/open-bus or ignored accesses that should not stop execution, (3) invalid hardware operations with documented status/error effects, and (4) actual SH-2 architectural exceptions. Avoid using an emulator implementation-gap error as a fabricated guest fault.

The browser must not halt *merely because* the firmware touches `+0x60` if the chosen, documented physical/revision behavior is nonfatal. Preserve useful optional developer diagnostics when behavior is uncertain. Do not generally mask unmapped memory, inappropriate widths, architectural address errors, legitimate register-specific errors or broken devices.

## Context and implementation guidance

- Start with `src/scu.rs` and `src/bus.rs` including cached `0x05FE0060` and cache-through `0x25FE0060`; inspect `src/cpu.rs` / `src/bus/transactions.rs` to distinguish direct 32-bit loads/stores, cache line-fill reads, DMA/device-initiated reads and generated bus cycles.
- Determine what the old and final SCU specs actually say for **writes and reads separately**. If the final spec explicitly forbids software writes but does not prescribe CPU termination, that is **not** license to synthesize a hardware exception. Carefully define deterministic fallback behavior for unsupported/removed register reads, with a stated uncertainty level; ensure that fallback is not silently generalized to other registers.
- Preserve existing DMA channel state, pending and in-progress transfers, scheduling, interrupts and triggers. A no-op write must not abort an actual transfer; a force-stop interpretation must implement its real state/deadline/IRQ consequences rather than only storing bits.
- Use a small shared access classification/diagnostic approach if genuinely needed; favor focused methods over broad abstractions or per-title compatibility hacks. Developer trace output must be bounded, opt-in, local and non-mutating. No special cases for BIOS PC, hashes, game identifiers or hand-authored fake startup screens.
- Keep SCU register aliases, register-width validation, true read-only/write-only rules, DMA bus ownership, and ST-210 fixes coherent with currently passing hardware tests.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Identify the exact failure and access origin:** with source-based native tests / a redistributable original synthetic 512 KiB BIOS, characterize reads vs writes at `+0x60`, 32-bit operand/aliases, and a cacheable access that may cause an indirect MMIO read. Improve diagnostics if needed to reveal direction, value, source/PC and whether the access was direct or generated. State explicitly that the actual private BIOS instruction is unavailable and cannot be classified from the original message.
- [ ] **Hardware-grounded compatibility decision:** compare the initial and final SCU specifications against Mednafen, Yabause, 5thPlanet and MAME. Record specific source sections and the confidence/limitations of selected read/write semantics. Do not conflate forbidden/documentation-undefined access with a measured CPU trap or with guaranteed DMA stop behavior.
- [ ] **Nonfatal behavior where supported:** implement the chosen bounded behavior for `+0x60` in the shared SCU/bus path so the original synthetic guest proceeds past its access (where the established policy permits it). Maintain optional, nonfatal diagnostics for undocumented use, rather than delivering a sticky `UnsupportedDevice` fault just because the model lacks an implemented function.
- [ ] **Correct DMA and status semantics:** test `+0x60` while all three DMA levels are idle, armed, pending, and active; check whether the selected policy should alter them, and assert exact effects / lack of effects on subsequent transfer data, DSTA/status, pending triggers, DMA IRQ, arbitration and cancellation. **Do not fabricate a DMA stop mechanism** without evidence. If a documented alternative (e.g. real channel disable) has different semantics, preserve that distinction.
- [ ] **Narrow safety controls:** unknown/unmapped regions and demonstrably unsupported widths, CPU address alignment violations, write-only/read-only register misuse, known SCU invalid transfer constraints, etc. still receive their distinct documented behavior or honest diagnostics; don't make an unconditional `Err => Ok(0)` for all MMIO and don't silently permit arbitrary writes. Ensure no global emulator exception swallowing.
- [ ] **Original end-to-end tests:** add native unit/bus and native reset-vector guest tests plus production Wasm/Chromium guest tests for 32-bit DSTP reads/writes, alias/cached access, repeated boots, media absent and present if applicable, and debug/status observability. Compare representative clocks/IRQ/transfer results across advancement chunks. Demonstrate failing-before/passing-after where a concrete defect is established. All test ROMs must be original and redistributable.
- [ ] **Preserve coverage:** existing SCU DMA/DSP, dual SH-2, BSC/cache, interrupts, BIOS-only Start, SMPC (including #109), CD, HLE, backup, video/audio, and ISO/CUE/BIN/CHD regressions remain passing. Do not modify guest code, expected results, or deadlines simply to hide the access.
- [ ] **Validation/documentation:** record actual source findings, unknown electrical behavior, changed files, before/after evidence and commands/results. Run the applicable locked Rust fmt/build/tests/Clippy, fixtures, production Wasm build, runner regressions and the complete browser suite according to `docs/development-flow.md` and `docs/ci-performance.md`. Require successful exact-head PR CI before merging; keep the aggregate artifact/publication barrier intact.

## Explicit non-goals

- Full stock Sega BIOS home menu, broad commercial-game compatibility and every unimplemented MMIO register.
- Automatically treating all future `UnsupportedDevice` faults as nonfatal.
- Copying code from another emulator, redistributing Sega firmware, or requiring the issue owner to provide their private BIOS.
- Blanket timeout/test relaxation or weakening diagnostics.

## Optional external BIOS verification

The requester will test their own legally obtained BIOS after publication. They may report whether the original `PC 0x0000181E` access still stops execution and the next fault if any. This is **not a pre-merge acceptance criterion**, as the implementer has no access to those bytes.

## Required post-merge verification

None required as a developer gate. User-led private BIOS testing is separate optional feedback.
